title: Ukrainian forces raise flag in Kupiansk as Russian front in Kharkiv region collapses
body:
On 10 September 2022, Reuters reported that Ukrainian troops had raised their flag in Kupiansk, a town in Kharkiv region where rail lines linking Russia to eastern Ukraine converge. Natalia Popova, an adviser to the head of the Kharkiv regional council, wrote that Kupiansk was Ukraine. Reuters said it could not independently verify the situation in the city.

The report described Izium as Russia's main stronghold and logistics base in the north-east and said Ukrainian advances threatened to encircle thousands of Russian troops there. Reuters said Russian forces had abandoned positions in evident haste, leaving ammunition and rubbish behind. Moscow acknowledged that its front in Kharkiv had buckled and said it was sending reinforcements.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said at least 30 settlements had been liberated. The report called the advance Ukraine's fastest since its defence of Kyiv in March 2022. The offensive had begun on 6 September, and Russia's Ministry of Defence announced a withdrawal from nearly all of Kharkiv Oblast on 11 September. The report also quoted regional police chief Volodymyr Tymoshenko, presidential office adviser Oleksiy Arestovych, Russian-installed administrator Vitaliy Ganchev and US Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin on the developments.
